Synopsis:
After Wulbren instigates the escape any escaping prisoners try to make it to the boat and flee Moonrise. This dialogue covers the case in which the boat leaves without the player or joins them in the escape.

Cluster Contexts:
- MOO_Jailbreak_Boat.json: The player is in the middle of a desperate jailbreak Wulbren helped organize: gnomes and captured tieflings are trying to reach the evac boat and flee Moonrise while the player is holding off cult forces. Wulbren Bongle — the imprisoned Ironhand leader who has been quietly directing the breakout — is telling the player to run the others to the boat and is about to board himself, which sparks the terse, emotional replies shown. Off‑screen the tower is on full alert (zealous half‑orc jailers, the Warden, and Disciple Balthazar’s orders), so escape is chaotic and the boat may either leave with Wulbren (possibly without the player) or take the player as well depending on the branch. The player’s lines reflect choices between staying to fight, accusing Wulbren of abandoning them, or ordering him to go for the greater good.
- MOO_NGB_Jailbreak_SpeakToPrisonerCrime.json: You’re in the Moonrise Towers cellblock trying to speak to prisoners when a scrying eye spots you and summons a guard; any guard can trigger this interruption, though it’s often the zealous, sadistic half‑orc jailer stationed here. The tower is on high alert after the recent Execution/Audience events, prisoners (tieflings and Ironhand gnomes among them) are tightly controlled, and the jailer can telepathically probe for tadpoles and report or escalate trouble to her superiors. Strict visitation rules are enforced: only Disciple Balthazar (or the Warden acting for him) may authorize conversations, so the player’s claim of permission is checked — pass and you may speak, fail and you’re brusquely dismissed with a warning (or worse). The guard’s reactions depend on your known associations and recent actions around Balthazar/Nightsong, so prior involvement can sway the outcome.
- Wyll_Leaving.json: Wyll informs you he is leaving the party
- TWN_Finale_LeavingAct.json: Scene of players leaving SCL to travel to Intermezzo. This scene triggers when the party leave Moonrise Tower after defeating Ketheric. There are two variants. One where the curse has been lifted, one where the curse hasn't been lifted.If the curse has been lifted, Halsin and/or Art Cullagh will be present at Moonrise if alive, and will tell players that the quest has succeeded, and that when they leave Moonrise, they'll see the restults. They tell you to wrap up your business here first. This happens in the dialogues for those characters, not here.If the curse hasn't been lifted, players see a vista of the shadow-cursed lands on leaving Moonrise, and move on toward the Risen Road.
- WYR_WyrmRockPrison_FlorrickOutisdeFortress.json: Florrick's dialog when you helped her leave the fortress.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Wulbren Bongle: There's no time! I'm leaving - hold them off. || [context] NodeContext: Yelling. Authorative and grave - he's about to flee while the player fights enemies off (node 42)
- Player: Stop talking and just go. (node 27)

Sample 2:
- Wulbren Bongle: There's no time! I'm leaving - hold them off. || [context] NodeContext: Yelling. Authorative and grave - he's about to flee while the player fights enemies off (node 42)
- Player: You ungrateful bastard, don't you dare leave. (node 11)

Sample 3:
- Wulbren Bongle: There's no time! I'm leaving - hold them off. || [context] NodeContext: Yelling. Authorative and grave - he's about to flee while the player fights enemies off (node 42)
- Player: Take the boat and go! They won't get past me. (node 57)

context: Wulbren Bongle—the Ironhand leader who quietly organized the breakout—has triggered a desperate jailbreak and is about to board the evac boat while the player holds off cult forces so prisoners (gnomes and captured tieflings) can reach safety. The Moonrise tower is on full alert (zealous half‑orc jailers, the Warden, orders from Disciple Balthazar), so the escape is chaotic and the boat may either leave with Wulbren (possibly without the player) or take the player as well depending on the branch. Wulbren’s shouted line reflects that he’s giving a curt, urgent order to flee; the player’s replies shown cover the plausible reactions—urging him to go for the greater good, accusing him of abandoning you, or insisting you’ll hold the line. Off‑screen pressure from pursuing guards and the need to shepherd other prisoners explain the terse, emotional exchange.
